newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean military disciplines 20 over submarine.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean military disciplines 20 over submarine.

text.p: Twenty South Korean military personnel face disciplinary action over the intrusion of a North Korean submarine in September that exposed gaping security holes and embarrassed South Korea's armed forces.

An announcement by the Joint Chiefs of Staff on Monday said the 20 faced disciplinary action for failures in guard duty, botching parts of the search for the 26 North Koreans agents who came ashore, and for friendly fire deaths during the hunt.
Two of the personnel face legal action, seven have been referred to disciplinary tribunals, three relieved of their duties and eight given warnings.
A review had exposed blind spots in South Korea's coastal defences and showed that a radar system to pick up submarine movements was inadequate, the statement said.
Tensions on the Korean peninsula have worsened since the North Korean submarine landed agents on a South Korean beach in September. Pyongyang says the incident was an accident.

The Shark-class vessel was spotted stranded on rocks off an east coast beach by a taxi driver. Of the 26 occupants, 24 were shot and killed during a search by tens of thousands of troops. One was captured alive and one is still missing.
In one friendly fire incident, a South Korean army corporal shot dead one of his officers after mistaking him for a Northern agent.
The two Koreas remain technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce, rather than a peace treaty.
